pr_title: Aggregated Discovery, mark APIServices stale before initial health check
pr_body:
/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Ensure all APIServices are present in Aggregated Discovery document before health check is completed.

I've moved the aggregator initialization earlier into `NewWithDelegate` instead of `PrepareRun`. I don't think there should be any impact/races by doing this.

- `AddPostStartHookOrDie` is always called after the initialization of the apiserver so creating a deferred function earlier should have no impact
- Moving `GenericAPIServer.AggregatedDiscoveryGroupManager.WithSource(aggregated.AggregatorSource)` earlier should be safe. The AggregatedDiscoveryGroupManager is initialized in `BuildGenericConfig` https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9c1c603fbef4abb1bfd257a02a32d7d16832a8a4/pkg/controlplane/apiserver/config.go#L165-L167 which is called before `NewWithDelegate` in the aggregator is called. (initialization goes through this path: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9c1c603fbef4abb1bfd257a02a32d7d16832a8a4/cmd/kube-apiserver/app/server.go#L152 while aggregator usage goes through https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9c1c603fbef4abb1bfd257a02a32d7d16832a8a4/cmd/kube-apiserver/app/server.go#L160

issue_context.title: Aggregated Discovery doesn't show aggregated apiservices as Stale before initial health check
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

[Quote from KEP 3352](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-api-machinery/3352-aggregated-discovery#aggregation):

> A post start hook will be added and the kube-apiserver health check should only pass if the discovery document is ready. Since aggregated api servers may take longer to respond and we do not want to delay cluster startup, the health check will only block on the local api servers (built-ins and CRDs) to have their discovery ready. For api servers that have not been aggregated, their group-versions will be published with an empty resource list and a Stale for Freshness to indicate that they have not synced yet.

This requirement is not met. Explanation in first comment shows we wait for local services to sync before health check, but we do not include aggregated apiservices that had not yet synced as Stale.

/cc @Jefftree @apelisse 
/sig api-machinery

### What did you expect to happen?

Unsynced aggregated APIServices which appear in the initial list for apiserver are included in document before health check with empty resource list and `Stale` freshness.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

N/A

comments:
I think for this one we almost have all our bases covered. For context, there is a single `AggregatedDiscoveryGroupManager` used by all of apiserver, apiextensions-apiserver, and aggregated-apiserver:

It is attached to genericConfig and the instance is shared by all three genericapiserver instances.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/201caf28b270d73c31b4f1f358548b1be608446c/cmd/kube-apiserver/app/server.go#L477-L479

For builtin types, the `genericapiserver` adds its types directly during initialization to the shared `AggregatedDiscoveryGroupManager ` when installing APIs, so there is no need to wait in a post-start hook for builtins:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/201caf28b270d73c31b4f1f358548b1be608446c/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/genericapiserver.go#L706-L712

For CRDs there is a post-start hook to wait for discovery controller to sync initial list of CRDs. This uses the same `AggregatedDiscoveryGroupManager` instance used by genericapiserver.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/60d73ba75148483d150622a4d8b6e122e189ceab/staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apiserver/apiserver.go#L213

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/60d73ba75148483d150622a4d8b6e122e189ceab/staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apiserver/apiserver.go#L250-L255

Aggregated APIServer also uses the same `DiscoveryResourceManager` and is not responsible for syncing any local APIServices.

The only thing missing from this requirement is that aggregated APIServices are not present in the initial document as `Stale`.

@alexzielenski please correct me if I'm missing something but isn't the purpose of `dirtyAPIServiceQueue` [field](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ed98c1da6d5fd1382a97663038c0fedbc02ebf9f/staging/src/k8s.io/kube-aggregator/pkg/apiserver/handler_discovery.go#L85) already adding APIServices as Stale?.

You summarized code navigation pretty well above, I started looking at the issue in case I can fix it, but I couldn't find the bug :)

Not sure if this was addressed but I'm going to make a pass on this and make sure it's fixed for GA.

/assign

review_comments: Is it possible that this blocks healthz until the requests for the aggregated apiservice discovery timeout? Is that the intended behavior? I had assumed we would allow startup to finish while these requests update in the background (but discovery reports their group-versions to be stale in the meantime)

Yes, discussed with deads2k. We're changing this to block until all aggregated apiservices are processed. At the moment the timeout is set to 5s (10s for aggregated apiservers under v1.26), so yes this may slightly slow down the time until an apiserver is ready.

noting for future-self that this means we have called `setInfoForAPIService` before this is closed, so every `discoveryManager.apiServices` that is known (lister hasSync is checked) is added and thus the `markInitialStale` will mark the starting list as stale.
With the new change, every apiservice will be processed and in discovery (either stale if unreachable or has all gvs)

I think this sort of thing needs an integration test instead. Make an aggregated APIservice that takes a long time to respond. The healthz shouldn't be up until you let your fake apiservice respond (but discovery should include it as stale).

I have a utlity in here somewhere that makes it easy to set up these sorts of integration tests:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/233949e05df3020c4ca58448343352d87f7a4493/test/integration/apiserver/discovery/discovery_test.go#L175-L212

This doesnt cause a problem here, but I think there is a pre-existing bug in WaitForGroups that may be worth fixing while we are here:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/233949e05df3020c4ca58448343352d87f7a4493/test/integration/apiserver/discovery/framework.go#L601-L612
